program_name: Veterinary Medicine — Italian official name: Corso di Laurea Magistrale a ciclo unico in “Medicina Veterinaria - Veterinary Medicine” (LM 42 R). The orientamento.unina.it page titles it “VETERINARY MEDICINE” and adds the flag “(in fase di accreditamento)”. It is a brand-new, fully English-taught single-cycle degree activated for the FIRST time in a.y. 2026/27 — it is not an English curriculum inside the existing Italian “Medicina Veterinaria” course, but a distinct degree programme with its own ministerial seat allocation and its own admission call. Awarded title on the orientamento page: “Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM)”. Reference department: Dipartimento di Medicina Veterinaria e Produzioni Animali (DMVPA / MVPA); School: Scuola di Agraria e Medicina Veterinaria (SAMV). Degree Programme Director: Prof. Livia D’Angelo (livia.dangelo@unina.it, +39 081 2536131). International/Erasmus contact: Prof. Laura Rinaldi (laura.rinaldi@unina.it). Student orientation contact: Prof. Marina Ceruso (marina.ceruso@unina.it). Practical-training contact: Prof. Maria Pia Pasolini.
level: Single-cycle (Laurea Magistrale a ciclo unico). Duration 5 years, 300 ECTS/CFU, 10 semesters, 29 exams. Breakdown published on the orientamento page: 12 ECTS elective activities, 35 ECTS practical evaluative training (30 mandatory + 5 elective), 10 ECTS final thesis. Under Law 163/2021 and Interministerial Decree 652/2022 the degree is directly professionally qualifying — graduates may practise as veterinarians with no separate state licensing exam (esame di Stato). NOTE: this is a 5-year / 300-CFU single-cycle degree, shorter than the 6-year / 360-CFU Medicine and Surgery (ENG) course at the same university.
teaching_language: English — “taught entirely in English”. The orientamento programme page lists “Language ENG” and “Language: English”, and the final thesis defence is “a public oral presentation in English”. Italian is NOT a teaching language and Italian B2 is NOT required: Federico II’s international pages state that for a single-cycle degree taught in English, “level B2 Italian language proficiency is not required”. However, Italian matters in practice: clinical rotations, the OVUD teaching veterinary hospital, the Frullone hospital for stray animals, ASL placements and livestock/dairy farms are Italian-speaking environments, and the programme itself states that “students are also offered the opportunity to acquire additional language skills (Italian language for non-native speakers) to enhance communication abilities and facilitate interaction in professional training environments.” The national admission test is written in English.
campus: Naples — Department of Veterinary Medicine and Animal Production, which operates on two sites listed on the programme page: (1) Complesso Frullone, Via Marco Rocco di Torrepadula 35, 80145 Napoli — the new campus where, per the university’s own 16 July 2026 news item, “classes will be held at the new Frullone campus”; (2) the historical building (sede storica), Via Federico Delpino 1, 80137 Napoli. Practical training takes place at the Ospedale Veterinario Universitario Didattico (OVUD) teaching veterinary hospital, the Frullone Veterinary Hospital for stray animals, the Clinical Skills Lab, necropsy/anatomy rooms, departmental laboratories, and affiliated farms, ASL public health authorities and private clinics. IMPORTANT — the admission test is NOT held at Frullone: the Naples test venue set by the bando is the Complesso Universitario di Monte S. Angelo, via Cinthia, Napoli. The student registry office is elsewhere again: Ufficio di Segreteria Studenti Area Didattica Medicina Veterinaria, via Tommaso De Amicis 95, Napoli (open Mon/Wed/Fri 09:00-12:00; Tue/Thu 09:00-12:00 and 14:30-16:30).
degree_class: LM-42 (Medicina Veterinaria). The 2026/27 admission decree and the ministerial programming write it as “LM 42 R” — the ‘R’ variant code used in the 2026/27 ministerial programming, exactly as ‘LM 41 R’ is used for the English Medicine course. The orientamento page shows plainly “Degree class LM-42”. Faculty/School: Agraria e Medicina Veterinaria. No public Federico II internal course code (of the ‘P11-DH6’ / ‘D24’ type) has yet been published for the English course — D24 / 18VE are the codes of the existing ITALIAN-taught Medicina Veterinaria, and the English programme’s own website is still “under construction”. [uncertain]
admission_type:
Restricted access (numero programmato nazionale) via the SEPARATE NATIONAL ADMISSION TEST FOR ENGLISH-TAUGHT HEALTH DEGREES — the IMAT-type route governed by MUR decree D.M. n. 1005 of 6 August 2026, “Definizione delle modalità e dei contenuti della prova di ammissione ai corsi di laurea magistrale a ciclo unico in Medicina e Chirurgia, Odontoiatria e Protesi Dentaria e Medicina Veterinaria, in lingua inglese - a.a. 2026/27”. 
RESOLUTION OF THE CRITICAL OPEN QUESTION (the same question flagged for Medicine and Surgery ENG): this programme does NOT go through the national ‘semestre filtro / semestre aperto’ (Legge 26/2025, D.M. 418/2025, D.M. 431/2025). Evidence, all from unina.it: (a) Federico II issued a dedicated 2026/27 competitive call for it, Decreto Rettorale DR/2026/3110 of 10/08/2026, signed by Rettore facente funzioni Angela Zampella, based on D.M. 1005/2026, with a written entrance exam on 29 September 2026 and answer sheets scored anonymously by CINECA; (b) the Federico II semestre filtro hub lists ONLY the Italian-taught courses — Medicina e Chirurgia (LM-41), Odontoiatria e Protesi Dentaria (LM-46), Medicina Veterinaria (LM-42) — and never mentions ‘lingua inglese’; (c) the filter-semester application window closed on 3 August 2026 (payment 6 August) and its lessons run from 1 September, which is structurally incompatible with a 29 September 2026 entrance exam; (d) the Veterinary English bando and the Medicine English bando appear side by side under ‘Corsi di laurea magistrale a ciclo unico’ on the Federico II numero-programmato page with identical documents and identical timing. So the answer is the same as for Medicine and Surgery (ENG): separate national English-language admission test, NOT the semestre filtro. 
There is ONE admission route for everyone — EU candidates, non-EU candidates legally resident in Italy, and non-EU candidates resident abroad all sit the same test on the same day; only the seat quota, the minimum score and the ranking authority differ (see seats and exam fields). There is no separate ‘international track’, no TOLC, no SAT, no portfolio and no interview.
academic_requirements:
Per art. 2 of bando DR/2026/3110, three eligible categories: (1) holders of an Italian upper-secondary school leaving diploma issued by an ‘istituto di istruzione secondaria di secondo grado’; (2) EU citizens wherever resident and non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy under art. 39 c.5 D.Lgs. 286/1998 as amended by art. 26 L. 189/2002, holding a foreign qualification obtained after AT LEAST 12 YEARS of schooling and recognised as equivalent to the Italian secondary diploma; (3) non-EU citizens resident abroad holding a foreign qualification obtained after at least 12 years of schooling and recognised as equivalent, following the MUR ‘Procedure per l’ingresso, il soggiorno, l’immatricolazione degli studenti internazionali’ valid for a.y. 2026/27 (www.studiare-in-italia.it). 
No prior university credits are needed — this is a single-cycle degree entered straight from secondary school. Subject preparation expected (orientamento page): “Candidates must also possess an adequate initial preparation, particularly in biology, chemistry, physics, and mathematics, in line with the national curricula for secondary schools”, i.e. the syllabus in Allegato A of D.M. 1005/2026. 
TRANSFERS AND SECOND-DEGREE CANDIDATES (art. 4): students seeking a passaggio from another Federico II course, a trasferimento from another university, and graduates of other degrees must ALL sit the same admission test and be placed in the ranking. Crucially, admitted candidates in these categories can be enrolled ONLY in the FIRST year, because a.y. 2026/27 is the first year the course exists: “gli ammessi saranno iscritti, solo ed esclusivamente, al primo anno … essendo l’a.a. 2026/27 il primo anno di attivazione del corso di studi in questione”. The Commissione di Coordinamento Didattico may recognise previously earned CFU, but enrolment above quota (sovrannumero) or outside the cohort is never permitted (points 12-15, Allegato 2, D.M. 1005/2026). Being declared ‘idoneo’ gives rights only in the current selection round, not in later years.
entry_exam_or_test:
YES — a single written national entrance examination for English-taught medical/veterinary degrees (the IMAT-type test), identical in content at every venue in Italy and abroad, governed by D.M. MUR n. 1005/2026 (Allegati 1, 2, 3, Tabella A, Allegato A). 
DATE AND VENUE: 29 September 2026, starting 13:30; candidates must be present at 11:30. Naples venue: Complesso Universitario di Monte S. Angelo, via Cinthia, Napoli; room assignments published the same day, candidates distributed by date of birth (twins excepted). No exception on the test venue is allowed; anyone arriving after the identification stage closes, or without a valid photo ID, is barred, and the fee is not refunded. The date was confirmed by a MUR ‘Errata corrige’ notice of 29 July 2026 (Direttore Generale Luisa A. De Paola), republished on unina.it, which explicitly covers Medicina e chirurgia, Odontoiatria e protesi dentaria AND Medicina veterinaria ‘erogati in lingua inglese’. 
FORMAT: 60 multiple-choice questions, 5 options each, in 100 minutes — 4 reading comprehension / general knowledge, 5 logical reasoning and problems, 23 biology, 15 chemistry, 13 physics and mathematics. Maximum 90 points: +1.5 per correct answer, -0.40 per wrong answer, 0 for no answer. 
MINIMUM SCORE: EU candidates and non-EU candidates legally resident in Italy must reach at least 20 points or they are declared ‘non idonei’ and are left out of the ranking. Non-EU candidates resident abroad are eligible with any score above zero (0); only those who answer nothing at all are excluded. 
TIE-BREAKS in order: biology, then chemistry, then physics & maths, then logical reasoning, then reading; then possession of an English language certification listed in Allegato 3 of D.M. 1005/2026 (self-declared at registration); then invalidity of 66% or more, or disability under L. 104/1992 art. 3 c. 3; then the younger candidate. 
PROCEDURE: sealed CINECA packs, anonymous barcode labels, answer sheets must not be signed (signing voids the test), black pen supplied by the university only; phones, smartwatches, tablets, earphones, bags, notes and any writing material are banned on pain of exclusion. Accommodations for disability (L. 104/1992, up to +50% time) and SLD/DSA (L. 170/2010, +30% time, non-scientific calculator, magnifier or reader) must be requested by PEC to area.studenti@pec.unina.it by 09/09/2026 15:00 with the medical certification; candidates resident abroad must supply their home-country certification with a sworn translation into Italian or English. 
TEST VENUES ABROAD (Tabella A of D.M. 1005/2026, relevant for non-EU candidates): Albania, Azerbaijan, Brazil, Canada, China, Cyprus, France, Germany, Greece, Hong Kong, India, Ireland, Kenya, Pakistan, Poland, Portugal, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Spain, Switzerland, Tunisia, TURKEY, UAE (Dubai), UK, USA — plus 18 Italian venues including Università di Napoli Federico II. Candidates who choose an Italian venue automatically sit the test at their first-preference university.
seats_total: 20 seats for a.y. 2026/27, split 18 + 2. Determined by the department’s potenziale formativo notice of 21.4.2026 (PG 50735/2026), approved urgently by D.R. n. 1582 of 28.4.2026, ratified by the Senato Accademico and Consiglio di Amministrazione on 29.5.2026, and confirmed in Tabella B of D.M. n. 1005/2026. Article 1 of bando DR/2026/3110 sets “20 posti”: 18 reserved for EU citizens and non-EU citizens resident in Italy, 2 reserved for non-EU citizens resident abroad. Unlike Medicine and Surgery (ENG) — whose quota was raised from 70 to 80 by D.R. 2792 of 20.7.2026 — NO later decree increasing the veterinary quota was found on unina.it as of 2026-08-30; the 20-seat figure in the 10 August 2026 bando is the current one. This is the smallest intake of any Federico II English-taught programme.
non_eu_reserved_seats: 2 seats only, reserved for non-EU citizens resident abroad (out of 20 total) — the single most restrictive fact about this programme for international applicants. The remaining 18 seats go to EU citizens and non-EU citizens legally resident in Italy. For these 2 reserved seats: (i) the eligibility threshold is any score above 0 rather than the 20-point minimum applied to the other category; (ii) the ranking is compiled by Federico II itself, not by CINECA (“La graduatoria dei candidati non comunitari residenti all’estero è definita da questo Ateneo con le stesse modalità sopra descritte”) and is published on www.unina.it; (iii) enrolment is done in person at the university offices rather than fully online. By comparison, Medicine and Surgery (ENG) at the same university reserves 45 seats for this category.
language_requirements:
TWO OFFICIAL UNINA STATEMENTS THAT DO NOT FULLY AGREE — both are quoted below. 
(a) PROGRAMME PAGES SAY B2 ENGLISH IS REQUIRED. The orientamento.unina.it programme page (marked ‘Aggiornata a.a. 2026/2027’) states: “A minimum level of English proficiency corresponding to B2 of the CEFR is required, typically achieved at the end of secondary education or through an equivalent qualification.” The university’s 16 July 2026 news item repeats that applicants must “demonstrate English proficiency at least at the B2 level according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR)”. 
(b) THE BINDING ADMISSION CALL IMPOSES NO CERTIFICATE. Bando DR/2026/3110 nowhere makes an English certificate a condition of participation or of enrolment. At registration on Universitaly the candidate merely DECLARES (self-certification under art. 46 D.P.R. 445/2000) whether he/she holds one of the certifications listed in Allegato 3 of D.M. 1005/2026, and that possession is used ONLY as a tie-breaker between candidates on equal scores. False declarations lead to cancellation of enrolment, recovery of benefits and forfeiture of fees paid. 
PRACTICAL READING: English proficiency is effectively tested by the exam itself, which is written entirely in English; no fixed IELTS/TOEFL score is published as a hard admission threshold, and no separate language test or interview is run by Federico II. Applicants should nevertheless obtain a B2-level certificate — it breaks ties, it matches what the programme pages say is expected, and Federico II explicitly notes that “an international certificate attesting to the level of English language skills (IELTS, TOEFL, Cambridge, etc.) is useful for the issue of the visa by the diplomatic/consular Representation.” 
ITALIAN: not required. Federico II’s admission regulation states that for a single-cycle degree taught in English “level B2 Italian language proficiency is not required”, and no Italian test is imposed at pre-enrolment. Italian language support courses for non-native speakers are offered during the programme for clinical placements.
application_deadline_eu:
For EU citizens and non-EU citizens legally resident in Italy (18 reserved seats), a.y. 2026/27, all dates from bando DR/2026/3110 and D.M. 1005/2026: 
• 2026-08-26 — admission-test registration OPENS on the Universitaly portal (www.universitaly.it), online only. 
• 2026-09-09, 15:00 (GMT+2) — registration CLOSES irrevocably, on pain of exclusion; the test contribution must also be paid via Universitaly. Venue preferences and the declared English certification are irrevocable and cannot be added after this moment; the last ‘conferma’ saved before the deadline counts. 
• 2026-09-09, 15:00 — same deadline for disability (L. 104/1992) / SLD (L. 170/2010) accommodation requests by PEC to area.studenti@pec.unina.it. 
• 2026-09-29, 13:30 — written admission test (present at 11:30). 
• 2026-10-08 — CINECA publishes anonymous scores by label code on Universitaly. 
• 2026-10-19 — candidates can view their own paper, score and registry form in the Universitaly reserved area. 
• 2026-10-26 — national nominative merit ranking published on Universitaly, with each candidate marked ASSEGNATO, PRENOTATO or IN ATTESA. 
• Enrolment window at each ranking release: maximum 4 days, excluding Saturdays and public holidays and including the day of the scorrimento. An ASSEGNATO candidate who misses it forfeits the place, whatever the reason. 
• Confirmation of interest in staying in the ranking: within 5 days of each release, by 12:00 of the fifth working day, in the Universitaly reserved area — no confirmation means removal from the national rankings. 
• 2026-11-03 — first scorrimento of the ranking; further scorrimenti repeat the same cycle until the ministerial closing decree. 
General Federico II fee/enrolment calendar for context (Guida all’iscrizione 2026-27): first instalment payable from 16 July (new enrolments) or 1 September and by 2026-11-02; late enrolment surcharges of 50 EUR from 2027-01-15 and 110 EUR from 2027-01-16. For this programme, however, the binding dates are the D.M. 1005/2026 ones listed above. 
NOTE: as of the capture date 2026-08-30 the registration window was OPEN (opened 26 August, closes 9 September 2026).
application_deadline_non_eu:
For non-EU citizens resident abroad (2 reserved seats), a.y. 2026/27: 
• Visa pre-enrolment on Universitaly (www.universitaly.it/studenti-stranieri): the Federico II general deadline was 2026-06-15, but the university states that “after this date pre-enrolment is allowed to the programmes with restricted access only” — which covers this programme, so pre-enrolment remains possible. 
• 2026-11-30 — deadline to submit the visa application at Italian Embassies/Consulates. 
• 2026-08-26 to 2026-09-09, 15:00 (GMT+2) — admission-test registration on Universitaly, the SAME single national procedure as for EU candidates. Candidates who wish to sit the test abroad must choose one of the overseas venues in Tabella A of D.M. 1005/2026 (Turkey is on that list). 
• 2026-09-29 — test date, identical worldwide. 
• Ranking: compiled by Federico II itself, not by CINECA, “with the same procedures”, and published on www.unina.it. The bando fixes no calendar date for it. 
• ENROLMENT DEADLINE: [uncertain] — art. 10 says only that non-EU candidates resident abroad must complete enrolment “entro e non oltre il termine che sarà reso noto con la pubblicazione della relativa graduatoria”, in person at the university offices that will be named when that ranking is published. As of 2026-08-30 no such date had been published. Expected late October / November 2026 by analogy with the national calendar. 
• After enrolling, the documentation submitted online must be printed and delivered within 15 days to the Segreteria Studenti Area Didattica Medicina Veterinaria, via Tommaso De Amicis 95, Napoli.
required_documents:
A. FOR THE ADMISSION TEST (art. 3 and art. 6 of the bando): online registration on Universitaly plus payment of the test contribution through Universitaly only. On test day the candidate must SHOW (exhibition only, no copies collected): (i) a valid photo identity document — identity card, photo driving licence, passport, postal card, state-issued ID card or firearms licence; (ii) the Universitaly test-registration receipt. Missing registration and/or payment means non-admission to the test and exclusion from the procedure. 
Candidates with invalidity/disability (L. 104/1992) must attach the certification issued by the territorially competent medical commission, in original or certified copy, stating the type of invalidity and degree of handicap, and specify the aid and extra time needed. Candidates with SLD/DSA (L. 170/2010) must attach a clinical DSA diagnosis in original or certified copy, issued no more than 3 years earlier OR after the candidate’s 18th birthday, from an SSN facility or a body/professional accredited with the Regional Health Service, including the functional profile — diagnoses without it are rejected. Candidates resident abroad must supply the equivalent certification from their country of residence with a sworn translation into Italian or English. Requests go by PEC to area.studenti@pec.unina.it using the form (‘Modulo per la richiesta di ausili o tempi aggiuntivi’) published alongside the bando. 
B. FOR ENROLMENT (art. 10): go to https://www.segrepass1.unina.it/Welcome.do, log in with codice fiscale + password or SPID, click ‘Accettazione posto in graduatoria’ under ‘Immatricolazioni - Corsi di Studio a numero programmato’, then ‘Immatricolazioni ai Corsi di Studio a numero programmato’, entering the self-certification of the school qualification and of family income (ISEEU), then pay the first instalment and the regional tax through the online carts. Bank transfers and post-office payments are NOT accepted, on pain of exclusion. Students transferring from another Federico II course must first be regularly enrolled for 2026/27 in their current course, then use ‘Passaggi’ > ‘Richiesta di passaggio’ and pay the passaggio fee. Non-EU candidates resident abroad enrol in person at the offices named with their ranking. All online documentation must be printed and delivered within 15 days to the Segreteria Studenti Area Didattica Medicina Veterinaria, via Tommaso De Amicis 95, Napoli. 
C. ADDITIONAL DOCUMENTS FOR NON-EU APPLICANTS (international.unina.it): validated Universitaly pre-enrolment summary; copy of passport; enrolment application form; 1 passport photo; Italian tax code (codice fiscale); proof of having applied for the residence permit; the foreign qualification with translation and legalisation plus either a Declaration of Value (DoV) from the Italian Embassy in the country where the qualification was obtained OR a certificate of comparability/validity from a CIMEA / ENIC-NARIC centre; health insurance for the visa. Federico II explicitly states: “The University of Naples Federico II does not issue admission letters for obtaining a visa.”
tuition_or_fees_link:
Links: https://www.unina.it/en/didattica/tasse-e-simulatore (Taxes and simulator, EN) · https://www.unina.it/it/didattica/iscrizioni-e-tasse (IT) · fee simulator http://calcolatrice.unina.it/ · binding 2026/27 guide ‘Guida all’iscrizione Anno accademico 2026-27’: https://www.unina.it/documents/d/guest/guida_studente_rapida_26-27_10-7-2026 · enrolment portal https://www.segrepass1.unina.it/Welcome.do. 
SUMMARY FOR 2026/27 (from the Guida): first-year students pay an ISEEU-based ‘contributo agevolato’ — fully exempt up to ISEEU 30,000 EUR; above that a fixed 1,011.50 EUR plus a variable component, to a maximum of 2,384.00 EUR for those who file no ISEEU declaration. Regional right-to-study tax: 130.00 EUR (ISEEU up to 25,500 EUR and students from particularly poor countries), 151.00 EUR (ISEEU 25,500.01-51,000 EUR AND students whose household resides abroad), 173.00 EUR (ISEEU above 51,000 EUR or no ISEEU declaration), plus 16.00 EUR stamp duty. 
DECISIVE FOR INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS: non-EU citizens are TOTALLY EXEMPT from the tuition contribution and pay only the regional tax plus stamp duty — realistically about 151 + 16 = 167 EUR/year for a student whose family lives abroad. Citizens of other EU countries pay a flat 200 EUR contribution plus regional tax and stamp duty. Instalments: 60% + regional tax + stamp duty from 16 July (new enrolments) or 1 September and by 2026-11-02; 20% by 2027-03-01; 20% by 2027-04-30; a 100 EUR surcharge applies from 2027-07-16 for unpaid 2nd/3rd instalments. The programme publishes no separate ‘international programme’ tuition — the standard university system applies.

uncertainty_notes:
1) CRITICAL QUESTION RESOLVED (high confidence, unina.it sources only). Veterinary Medicine (ENG) follows the SAME route as Medicine and Surgery (ENG): the separate national admission test for English-taught health degrees under D.M. MUR 1005/2026, with its own Federico II call DR/2026/3110 of 10/08/2026 and a test on 29 September 2026. It does NOT go through the semestre filtro / semestre aperto. Supporting evidence: the semestre filtro hub lists only the three Italian-taught courses and never says ‘lingua inglese’; its application window closed on 3 August 2026, before the English bando was even published (10 August 2026); its lessons started 1 September, incompatible with a 29 September test; the MUR errata corrige of 29 July 2026 names Medicina veterinaria ‘erogati in lingua inglese’ among the courses whose test falls on 29 September 2026. No conflicting official unina.it statement was found. 
2) ACCREDITATION STATUS — STILL FORMALLY FLAGGED, BUT PRACTICALLY GOING AHEAD. The orientamento page, although marked ‘Aggiornata a.a. 2026/2027’, still carries the label ‘Veterinary Medicine (in fase di accreditamento)’ as of 2026-08-30. Against that, three strong signals that the course is being activated: (a) MUR assigned it seats in Tabella B of D.M. 1005/2026 (18 + 2); (b) Federico II published a full 24-page competitive call for it on 10 August 2026 with a live registration window; (c) the bando itself states that a.a. 2026/27 is ‘il primo anno di attivazione del corso di studi’. No explicit unina.it decree removing the ‘in fase di accreditamento’ wording was found, so a residual formal risk cannot be excluded and the label is reported as published. 
3) THE DECISIVE PRACTICAL CONSTRAINT IS THE 2-SEAT NON-EU QUOTA, not the seat total. Only 2 of the 20 seats are open to non-EU candidates resident abroad (e.g. Turkish applicants applying from Turkey). This makes the programme far harder to enter from outside the EU than Medicine and Surgery (ENG) at the same university, which reserves 45 seats for the same category. Anyone who is an EU citizen, or legally resident in Italy, competes instead for the 18-seat quota but must clear the 20-point minimum score. 
4) ENGLISH REQUIREMENT — CONFLICTING OFFICIAL WORDING. The orientamento page and the 16 July 2026 university news both state that B2 CEFR English ‘is required’, while the binding bando DR/2026/3110 imposes no certificate at all and uses the Allegato 3 certifications only as a tie-breaker. The safest reading: no certificate blocks your application, but hold a B2-level certificate anyway (tie-break value, consistency with the programme description, and visa usefulness). No named threshold (e.g. IELTS 6.0) is published anywhere on unina.it for this programme. 
5) NON-EU ENROLMENT DEADLINE UNKNOWN. The bando fixes no date for enrolment of non-EU candidates resident abroad; it will be announced together with the university-compiled ranking (expected late October / November 2026). Marked [uncertain] in application_deadline_non_eu. Likewise the publication date of that university-compiled ranking is not fixed in the call. 
6) NO PROGRAMME MICROSITE / COURSE CODE YET. The orientamento page says the degree programme website is ‘under construction’, and no Federico II internal course code for the English course has been published; https://www.corsi.unina.it/D24 and the code 18VE belong to the ITALIAN-taught Medicina Veterinaria, which is entered through the semestre filtro and must not be confused with this programme. Marked [uncertain] in degree_class. 
7) SEAT COUNT STABILITY. Medicine and Surgery (ENG) had its quota raised from 70 to 80 by a later decree (D.R. 2792 of 20.7.2026). No equivalent increase decree was found for Veterinary Medicine; 20 (18 + 2) is what the 10 August 2026 bando and Tabella B of D.M. 1005/2026 both state. A later Federico II notice could still change this. 
8) CAMPUS. The task brief says ‘Frullone’, which is confirmed for teaching (‘Classes will be held at the new Frullone campus’, 16/07/2026 news) — but the department formally operates on two sites (Frullone and the historical Delpino building), the admission test is at Monte S. Angelo, and the student registry is on via Tommaso De Amicis. 
9) DEGREE NAME. The Italian official name is a bilingual compound, ‘Medicina Veterinaria - Veterinary Medicine’ (LM 42 R); this is a standalone English degree, not an English curriculum of the Italian course, so the diploma should carry that name rather than a purely Italian one. The awarded title as published is ‘Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM)’.

Test registration was OPEN at capture time (26 August – 9 September 2026), so ranking dates, the non-EU enrolment deadline and any accreditation update may still be published later on www.unina.it.
